subject: System Design
title: When to Use a Simple File
description: A quick, practical guide to When to Use a Simple File.

hook.text: A startup spends weeks setting up a database. Their data fits in a single CSV file.

buildup.text: Files, CSVs, and JSON are perfectly valid storage for small datasets, config, and static content.

discovery.text: SQLite handles millions of rows in a single file with full SQL support. No server required.

twist.text: Many successful products launched with flat files or SQLite and only moved to a database when they truly needed it.

climax.text: The simplest storage that meets your requirements is the right choice. Don't over-engineer data storage.

punchline.text: Sometimes a file is the best database.

quiz.question: When is a file or SQLite a good choice for data storage?
options: When the dataset is small and access patterns are simple
When you have millions of concurrent users
